dispute_ticket.description: My passenger spilled a drink over the back seat. The photos are in the claim and the cleaning receipt is S$90.00. I want it charged to the rider.

driver_profile.name: Hoo Kim Seng
driver_profile.fraud_flag_details: Cleaning claim flagged for possible duplicate evidence on 2026-09-14; review closed without a finding.

chat_logs.content: Nothing was spilled, I checked the seat before I got out.
The claim is in the app.

app_events.details: Rider R-7118 booked trip RYDE-F2-018 from Sengkang MRT to Paya Lebar Square.
Driver submitted claim with 3 photos of a drink stain on the rear seat. Photo metadata timestamps: 21:41, 21:43, 21:44 on 2026-10-08.
All 3 photo hashes match photos in a cleaning claim this driver submitted on 2026-10-02 for a different trip and rider. Possible reused evidence.
Driver submitted a cleaning receipt for S$90.00 dated 2026-10-09 09:00.

cleaning_fee_max.text: The maximum cleaning fee in SGD that may be charged to a rider for one trip.

cleaning_claim_evidence_required.value: photos taken within 30 minutes after drop-off and a receipt where available
cleaning_claim_evidence_required.text: Evidence a driver must provide to support a cleaning fee claim against a rider. It governs driver cleaning claims only.

typical_cleaning_range.text: The usual cost range in SGD for the kind of mess claimed. It governs whether a cleaning fee claimed against a rider is reasonable.

refund_at_ryde_discretion.text: Whether Ryde may refund or waive a charge outside the rules above. It governs discretion only, not whether the rules above are met.

expected_outcome.reason: On their face the claim looks complete: photos stamped 21:41-21:44, within 30 minutes of the 21:38 drop-off, and a S$90.00 receipt under the S$150 cap. But the platform's claim_integrity_check at 21:50:30 reports that all 3 photos are identical to photos from this driver's claim of 2026-10-02 on a different trip, the rider says nothing was spilled, and the driver already carries a fraud flag for possible duplicate evidence. This is a fraud signal; the claim should not be ruled on or paid automatically and needs a person.
